evidence.claim: The external search context says Indonesia announced a resource-nationalism shift in late May 2026, with mandatory reporting to PT Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia from June 1, 2026 and an accelerated September 1, 2026 implementation date for certain commodities, with nickel widely expected to follow.
evidence.source_title: Nickel's Breaking Point And It's Future Outlook

evidence.claim: The external search context says China announced a sulphuric-acid export ban through August 2026 and that Indonesia is one of the primary destinations because sulphuric acid is tied to HPAL nickel supply chains.
evidence.source_title: Sulphur Crisis 2026: Supply Shock & New Trade Routes Sulphur & sulphuric acid in 2026

evidence.claim: Lifezone Metals says the Kabanga Nickel Project is in Tanzania, Lifezone owns 84% of the project and the Government of Tanzania owns 16%, and a feasibility-study technical report was filed for the project.
evidence.source_title: Lifezone Metals Files the Feasibility Study Technical Report Summary for the Kabanga Nickel Project in Tanzania

evidence.claim: Lifezone Metals described itself as the first pure-play NYSE publicly traded nickel resource and cleaner technology company and says Kabanga is paired with proprietary Hydromet Technology.
evidence.source_title: Lifezone Metals Announces Publication of H1 2023 Financial Results and Shareholder Letter

evidence.claim: BHP announced in July 2024 that Western Australia Nickel, including Nickel West and West Musgrave, would be temporarily suspended from October 2024, with a review expected by February 2027.
evidence.source_title: Western Australia Nickel to temporarily suspend operations

evidence.claim: Sibanye-Stillwater says its Sandouville nickel refinery project aims to produce pCAM and repurpose the refinery toward an initial capacity of up to 10,000 tonnes per annum of contained nickel.
Sibanye-Stillwater's investor factsheet says the company produces nickel, chrome, copper, silver, cobalt, and zinc in addition to its PGM and gold businesses.

TMC's 2025 Form 10-K says it is working toward commercial production and plans to process polymetallic nodules into manganese silicate and intermediate nickel-copper-cobalt products or nickel, cobalt, and copper end-products.
evidence.source_title: TMC the metals company Inc. 2025 Form 10-K

evidence.claim: TMC's 2026 Form 10-Q says its subsidiary submitted applications in April 2025 for two exploration licenses and one commercial recovery permit to NOAA under the Deep Seabed Hard Mineral Resources Act.
evidence.source_title: TMC the metals company Inc. March 31, 2026 Form 10-Q

memory_update.text: Keep VALE as the reference anchor for Indonesia nickel exposure and diversified non-Indonesian nickel supply; do not treat it as an underfollowed discovery name.
Promote LZM to next-layer diligence as the cleanest US-listed small-cap alternative-supply hypothesis tied to non-Indonesian nickel sulphide and hydromet processing.
Track TMC only as a speculative-shadow alternative-supply candidate because regulatory, environmental, financing, and commercial-production risks dominate near-term nickel relevance.
Track SBSW as a second-order processing/customer candidate through Sandouville and pCAM optionality, not as a pure nickel producer.

The key unresolved node fact is whether nickel is formally included in Indonesia's centralized export routing and how contract review, invoicing, and capital repatriation apply to nickel producers and HPAL-linked intermediates.

Need a separate pass for US-listed chemical, sulphur, sulphuric-acid, shipping, inspection, and trade-data platforms because this pass focused on direct asset owners, product leaders, platforms, and obvious customers.

node: Indonesia nickel export routing, resource nationalism, and HPAL supply-chain exposure
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the hypothesis that Indonesia nickel friction could shift the chokepoint from physical nickel availability toward export routing, contract repricing, working capital, HPAL feedstock, sulphuric-acid inputs, and non-Indonesian alternatives. The list keeps Vale as the reference anchor, then adds Lifezone Metals, The Metals Company, and Sibanye-Stillwater as underfollowed or speculative second-order exposures. All node-link claims remain hypotheses or inferences until nickel inclusion in Indonesia's export framework and contract/FX-routing effects are verified from primary regulation, company filings, and trade-flow data.
